key_insight: In a multi-step coding setting, the researchers identify a small set of attention heads whose outputs encode the model’s next sub-goal. This suggests that some upcoming objectives can be read from internal activity before they are carried out.
problem_solved: Determining whether LLMs internally represent goals that guide future actions, rather than merely producing behavior that appears goal-directed.
method: Construct a coding environment with multiple sub-tasks to evaluate goal-seeking behavior and sub-goal selection.
Analyze attention-head outputs to locate internal representations of the next sub-goal.
Identify a sparse set of heads that carries information about the model’s upcoming objective.
impact: The findings suggest a route toward inspecting an LLM’s upcoming sub-goals, potentially improving interpretability and behavioral monitoring. The supplied abstract is truncated, so broader claims about predictive accuracy or generalization remain unspecified.
visual_elements: Task tree showing one coding goal branching into several possible sub-goals and execution paths.
Transformer schematic highlighting the small set of attention heads associated with sub-goal encoding.
Timeline showing internal sub-goal representation preceding task execution.
Conceptual flow diagram: attention-head outputs → decoded sub-goal → upcoming action.
paper_authors: Arnab Sen Sharma, Eric Todd, Sheridan Feucht, Andy Arditi, Rohit Gandikota
